architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

core_scientific_tool.name: get_state_aware_rheology_summary
core_scientific_tool.role: Convert the paper's upstream findings into machine-usable design rules without exposing the validation formulation or its outcome.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities
reproducibility of the recommendation under the same evidence contract
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 mitigates the established thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure in the local formulation family rather than merely changing initial viscosity.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: After verified formulation closure and matched documented processing, the median candidate SI across at least two independent realization or process-history replicates must be lower than the E5 reference SI at both 15-60 min and 15-90 min, with the complete 120 C trajectory reported and no credit assigned solely for a changed initial viscosity. E1-level SI values of 0.095 and 0.168 are favorable secondary benchmarks, not mandatory pass thresholds.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: The experiment fails if median SI is not lower than the E5 reference at either adjudication window, if improvement is attributable only to an unreported or unmatched initial-viscosity or thermal-equilibration difference, if stoichiometric or process-history records are incomplete, or if replicate behavior is inconsistent enough to prevent an interpretable comparison.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: Temperature sweep over 80-130 C with a 120 C state anchor; thermal hold at 120 C over 15-90 min with readings at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min and SI adjudication at 15-60 and 15-90 min.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Full dual-axis coverage with lower total modifier burden, but its 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the repeatedly supported approximately 4.8-6.4 wt% minor-resin region; retain as the minimum-burden comparator.
Full coverage and stronger acrylic perturbation, but higher acrylic burden may increase initial-viscosity and processing confounding while the tackifier remains at 2.5 wt%.
Lowest-burden full-coverage probe, but 10 wt% acrylic is below the conservative 15-20 wt% acrylic evidence band and may yield a weakly informative negative result.
Useful matched no-modifier control, but it zeroes both independently supported intervention axes and therefore cannot serve as the performance-mitigation experiment.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: The physical failure mode is formulation-dependent viscosity drift during the 120 C hold, not merely static viscosity level. Local experiments establish the E1/E5 hold contrast and show that process state can shift viscosity scale substantially; the state-aware rheology rule therefore requires an in-range sweep, a 120 C state anchor, full hold trajectories, and independent realization replication. Paper-derived rheological evidence supports separating static viscosity, temperature response, and temporal hold stability, and supports using one-point calibration only as a validated local-family correction rather than as an exact predictor. Curated PUR literature supports an acrylic-like formulation family, a broad directional acrylic region around 15-25 wt%, and a minor tackifier region centered near approximately 5 wt%, but does not predict S1C41's wet-lab outcome or establish a molecular mechanism. The conservative experimental-design rule for performance mitigation requires coverage of both independently supported axes before using modifier burden as a tie-break. S1C41 therefore tests 15 wt% acrylic-like modifier plus 5 wt% minor tackifier-like modifier on the E2 reactive-core anchor: it retains full coverage and uses the better-supported tackifier level. This resolves the Robustness Adjudicator's concern about the weaker 2.5 wt% tackifier level in S1C40, while accepting the small additional modifier burden as justified for the primary performance test. S1C40 remains the lower-burden comparator, and S1C45 remains a higher-acrylic alternative, but neither is preferred for the single primary experiment. The Skeptic's objections are resolved by making stoichiometric verification and complete process-history documentation preconditions, treating modified-chemistry state calibration as extrapolative, requiring at least two independent realizations, comparing full trajectories rather than endpoints, and replacing the unsupported mandatory E1-level threshold with improvement relative to the E5 reference at both SI windows. The dual-modifier result must not be interpreted as causal attribution of either axis.

action_requests.reason: Canonical upstream bridge required before candidate comparison. Confirm the formulation-only versus state-aware model result, state-shift master-curve structure, one-point calibration value, local apparent temperature-sensitivity coordinate, E1/E5 hold contrast, and the resulting measurement rules.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve the original lower-drift reference trajectory and deterministic SI descriptors for comparison with any mitigation candidate.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the original high-drift failure trajectory that defines the performance-mitigation target.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: Quantify the realization/process-state uncertainty before treating a nominal temperature-sweep viscosity as a material property or using it as the primary candidate objective.

action_requests.name: get_candidate_hypothesis
action_requests.reason: After the local failure mode and objective are established, obtain the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, E2 reactive-core anchor, independent acrylic and tackifier axes, and historical/claim boundary without treating it as an optimum.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Retrieve source-level chemistry evidence to support plausible modifier directions and bounded regions. Use acrylic percentages as directional/noncommensurate anchors and comparative stability reports as hypotheses, not as exact local targets.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Initial viscosity level at an anchor temperature within the measured 80-130 C range
Thermal-hold SI over 15-60 min and 15-90 min at 120 C
Absolute and relative viscosity trajectory during the hold, not only the endpoint
Temperature-response slope or state-aware apparent temperature sensitivity over measured support
Consistency with the state-shift master-curve and one-point calibration result
Repeatability across independent realization or process-history replicates
Acrylic modifier fraction and functionality region relative to directly or directionally supported evidence
Minor tackifier fraction and identity region relative to bounded evidence
Reactive-core stoichiometry, MDI balance, total formulation closure, and feasible processing viscosity
Extrapolation distance from measured chemistry, temperature, time, and process-state support
Evidence coverage and uncertainty penalty, including process-history and measurement uncertainty
counterfactual_checks: Would the candidate still be preferred if candidates were compared at matched initial viscosity rather than matched composition?
Would the conclusion remain if the E2 repeatability spread were treated as process-state uncertainty rather than random measurement noise?
Does the candidate reduce the 120 C hold SI relative to E5 without sacrificing feasibility or moving outside measured support?
Is any apparent improvement explained solely by a lower starting viscosity or by a different thermal equilibration history?
Would an acrylic-only or tackifier-only intervention provide comparable mitigation, and is the multi-component intervention justified by the declared performance-mitigation intent?
Does the result depend on treating an external 15%, 20%, or 25% modifier percentage as an exact optimum rather than as directional analogue evidence?
If state calibration is omitted, does the candidate ranking change materially across the measured temperature range?
Could the observed response be attributed only to formulation-family behavior and not to a specific molecular mechanism?
planner.decision_goal: Select one pre-result candidate experiment that mitigates the established thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure while remaining within measured temperature support, bounded evidence-supported modifier regions, and explicit stoichiometric and process-history constraints.
design_implications: The next experiment should optimize hold-stability response, not only a single nominal viscosity at one temperature.
Measure both initial viscosity level and viscosity trajectory during the hold so a lower starting viscosity is not incorrectly credited for improved stability.

Use a state-aware model or one-point state calibration if the upstream rheology summary confirms that state shifts collapse the temperature sweeps; preserve realization and process-history uncertainty in interpretation.

Use the 120 C hold temperature and 15-90 min interval because they are directly supported by the original measurements; avoid extrapolating the hold criterion to longer times or unsupported temperatures.

A multi-component acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier intervention is admissible for performance mitigation because both modifier axes have independent external support, provided each remains within the bounded candidate lattice and stoichiometric feasibility is checked.

Treat approximately 15-20 wt% acrylic as a directional analogue region and approximately 2.5-10 wt% tackifier as a conservative minor-modifier region; do not convert these literature values into an exact local optimum.

Directly commensurate local numeric anchors are the E1/E5 hold SI values at 120 C over 15-60 and 15-90 min. External acrylic and tackifier percentages are noncommensurate analogue anchors, while upper bounds and measured-range-only policies are conservative extrapolation controls.
Do not claim a molecular mechanism from rheology alone; describe modifier effects as formulation-family or functionality hypotheses requiring candidate-specific measurement.
material_regularities_to_use: All available temperature sweeps for E1, E2, and E3 decrease monotonically with temperature over the measured 80-130 C range.
E1 and E2 show similar descriptive Andrade temperature-response slopes, so nominal viscosity level and temperature sensitivity should not be treated as interchangeable objectives.

E2 temperature-sweep repeatability is poor descriptively, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum-to-minimum ratios approximately 2.8-3.6 across 80-130 C; run and process state may materially affect apparent viscosity.
The original thermal-hold data show a strong formulation-dependent stability contrast at 120 C over the measured 15-90 min window.

External evidence supports acrylic-modified PUR and minor tackifier-containing PUR as plausible formulation families, but it does not establish the local optimum or directly match the local hold protocol.
The candidate lattice is historical and pre-result; candidate identity, order, and any later validation outcome must not be inferred from it.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold viscosity drift is the primary established failure mode: at 120 C, E5 shows much larger relative viscosity growth than E1 over both 15-60 min (SI 0.515 versus 0.095) and 15-90 min (SI 0.931 versus 0.168). This must be distinguished from the separate high realization/process-state uncertainty indicated by the E2 temperature-sweep spread.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Temperature sweep over the measured 80-130 C support with at least one-point state calibration if required by the state-aware summary
Initial viscosity at the selected anchor temperature before the hold
Thermal-hold viscosity trajectory at 120 C over 15-60 and 15-90 min, with SI computed as (eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0
Intermediate hold readings sufficient to distinguish early drift from approximately linear or accelerating drift
At least one independent repeat or explicitly documented process-history replicate
Composition and stoichiometric records for polyol, acrylic-like modifier, tackifier-like modifier, and MDI fractions
Processing history, conditioning time, temperature equilibration, measurement geometry, and run-order metadata
A comparison against the original E1/E5 hold descriptors using preserved source units and the same hold schedule
uncertainty_triggers: The state-aware summary does not support a stable state-shift correction or one-point calibration
Candidate temperature or hold time lies outside the measured 80-130 C and 15-90 min support
Candidate composition requires acrylic or tackifier levels beyond the bounded lattice or lacks stoichiometric closure
Initial viscosity changes substantially while hold SI does not improve, making apparent mitigation a viscosity-level artifact
A single run shows improvement but repeatability remains comparable to the large E2 spread
Process history, conditioning, or thermal equilibration differs materially from the original reference measurements
External evidence is only directional, lacks matched chemistry, or reports incompatible units or endpoints
Candidate behavior is dominated by an unmeasured phase, cure, mixing, or handling effect that rheology alone cannot identify

provisional_acceptance_criterion.claim: The candidate mitigates the established thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure rather than merely changing initial viscosity.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.criterion: Across at least two independent realization or explicitly documented process-history replicates, the candidate's median SI should be lower than the E5 reference at both windows and provisionally no greater than the lower-drift E1 references of 0.095 over 15-60 min and 0.168 over 15-90 min, while initial viscosity and the full trajectory are reported for confounding assessment.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Failure is declared if SI is not reduced relative to E5, if improvement occurs only through a substantially altered initial viscosity without trajectory improvement, or if replicate spread is comparable to the large E2 process-state spread and prevents an interpretable conclusion.
provisional_acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C over 15-90 min, with SI adjudicated at 15-60 and 15-90 min

provisional_measurement_plan.primary_response: Matched 120 C thermal-hold viscosity trajectory with SI computed over 15-60 min and 15-90 min, including intermediate readings at 15, 30, 60, and 90 min; report initial viscosity separately and compare against E1/E5 using preserved units and schedule.
provisional_measurement_plan.state_anchor_plan: Run a temperature sweep over the measured 80-130 C range and obtain at least one state-specific viscosity anchor at 120 C before or at the start of the hold. Preserve mixing history, conditioning time, equilibration, geometry, run order, and sample age. Include at least one independent process-history or realization replicate; use one-point state calibration only if the candidate remains within the supported local response family.
provisional_measurement_plan.time_window: 15-90 min, with required adjudication at both 15-60 min and 15-90 min

regularities_used: Measured local evidence: E5 has much larger 120 C viscosity drift than E1, with SI 0.515 versus 0.095 over 15-60 min and 0.931 versus 0.168 over 15-90 min.
Measured local evidence: hold trajectories are approximately linear in ln(viscosity), so intermediate time points can distinguish early, linear, and accelerating drift.
Measured local evidence: E2 temperature-sweep repeatability is poor, with CV approximately 0.46-0.58 and maximum-to-minimum ratios up to approximately 3.57 at 120 C.
Derived model rule: realization/process state primarily shifts viscosity scale while a common temperature-response shape remains transferable after one-point state calibration.
Derived decision rule: static viscosity, temperature response, and hold stability are separate objectives; static viscosity must not substitute for the matched hold measurement.

External analogue evidence: acrylic-like PUR formulations support a broad directional region around 15-25 wt% acrylic-like modifier, with repeated analogue examples near 20 wt% and comparative stability evidence at 25 wt%.
External analogue evidence: minor tackifier-like PUR formulations cluster near approximately 5 wt%, with conservative guidance below about 10 wt%.
Conservative design principle: for performance mitigation, both independently supported intervention axes must be covered before minimum modifier burden is used as a tie-break.

Unresolved uncertainty: external modifier percentages and stability results are not directly commensurate with the local AC1920/TK100 chemistry or hold protocol and do not establish an exact optimum or molecular mechanism.
proposer.scientific_target: Mitigate thermal-hold viscosity drift at 120 C over the directly supported 15-60 and 15-90 min windows while separating formulation effects from realization/process-state effects.
unresolved_questions: Does the combined acrylic-like plus minor tackifier-like intervention reduce hold drift in the local chemistry, or does it primarily shift viscosity scale?
Is S1C40's lower total modifier burden sufficient, or is the 5 wt% tackifier-like level in S1C41 required for robust mitigation?
Does increasing acrylic-like modifier from 15 to 17.5 wt% improve matched-hold SI, and can that effect be distinguished from processing and initial-viscosity changes?
Can one-point state calibration remain accurate for the modified candidates, given that the state-aware model was audited only within the original local chemistry family?
Do candidate-specific process fields, material specifications, and reactive functionality require recalculation of true NCO:OH stoichiometry?
Which response differences remain after independent realization replication and matched thermal equilibration?
The evidence supports a modifier family and a bounded region, not an exact composition or molecular mechanism.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Provides full coverage at 15 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier, matching the repeated tackifier analogue region, but adds burden and may increase initial-viscosity or processing confounding.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The experiment prioritizes stronger independent support for the tackifier axis over minimizing total modifier burden.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Retains full coverage but increases acrylic burden to 17.5 wt% while keeping the weakly supported 2.5 wt% tackifier level.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A larger acrylic perturbation is needed to test whether the lower 15 wt% acrylic level is insufficient.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Full coverage with lower total burden, but 10 wt% acrylic is below the conservative supported acrylic band and a negative result would be weakly informative.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: The primary goal is a minimum-perturbation uncertainty probe rather than the strongest mitigation test.

alternative_comparison.scientific_tradeoff: Cleaner baseline control but does not test the full performance-mitigation strategy and should not replace a full-coverage performance candidate.
alternative_comparison.would_be_preferred_if: A matched no-modifier control is required to separate modifier-family effects from reactive-core and process-state behavior.

required_conditions: Verify modifier functionality and recalculate formulation closure and true NCO:OH stoichiometry before testing.
Document all missing process-history, conditioning, equilibration, geometry, sample-age, and run-order fields.
Use improvement relative to E5 at both SI windows as the primary success criterion; treat E1-level SI as a secondary benchmark.
Prespecify allowable initial-viscosity differences and compare full trajectories, not only endpoint SI.
Run at least two independent realization or process-history replicates and define a numerical rule for process-state-confounded results.
Include the 80-130 C sweep and 120 C state anchor, while labeling state calibration for the modified chemistry as an extrapolation requiring validation.
If only one candidate can be run, select S1C41 over S1C40 because its dual-axis coverage is retained while the tackifier level is independently better supported.
Do not interpret the dual-modifier result as identifying acrylic-versus-tackifier causality.

robustness_checks.detail: S1C40 directly tests the established 120 C thermal-hold viscosity-drift failure using both 15-60 min and 15-90 min SI windows.
The Planner declares performance_mitigation, for which a dual-axis intervention is appropriate; S1C40 covers both independently supported axes.
S1C40 retains full axis coverage when exact analogue-distance rewards are removed, but its 2.5 wt% tackifier level is below the repeatedly supported approximately 4.8-6.4 wt% region.

S1C41 provides the same 15 wt% acrylic coverage with 5 wt% tackifier in the better-supported minor-resin region, at only 2.5 percentage points greater total modifier burden; it is a credible robustness comparator and may be preferred if evidential sufficiency is prioritized over minimum burden.
No partial-coverage candidate is promoted solely because it has lower modifier burden. S1C40 is full coverage.

Six process fields are missing, modifier functionality is unresolved, and true NCO:OH stoichiometry must be recalculated before interpretation. State-aware calibration was audited only within the original local chemistry family.

The proposed sweep, 120 C trajectory, intermediate readings, state anchor, and replicate are appropriate, but quantitative rules for matched initial viscosity, replicate spread, calibration failure, and thermal equilibration deviations remain unspecified.
Treating the single E1 realization as a mandatory SI threshold is stronger than the evidence supports. Improvement relative to E5 should be primary; E1-level SI should be a secondary benchmark.

The recommendation does not depend on exact literature-distance scores, but it depends on the conservative assumption that both supported axes should be included and on extrapolating state calibration to a modified chemistry family.

The Skeptic identified serious interpretability problems requiring explicit preconditions and revised criteria, but not grounds for abstention because the failure mode, full-coverage candidate class, and direct adjudication measurements are clear.

counterfactual_failures: The proposal does not specify a matched-initial-viscosity analysis rule or allowable initial-viscosity difference, so the conclusion could still be influenced by a starting-level artifact.
The proposal acknowledges E2 process-state uncertainty but does not define how candidate SI will be compared with that uncertainty before declaring mitigation.

S1C40 versus S1C41 changes tackifier loading while retaining acrylic loading, but the experiment plan does not clearly state whether both ranked points will be run; if only S1C40 is run, tackifier sufficiency remains unresolved.

The full-coverage rule prevents an acrylic-only or tackifier-only candidate from being the performance rank-1, but the supplied evidence does not establish that both axes are required for local mitigation.
The proposal does not prescribe a formal sensitivity analysis for omitting state calibration or for deviations in thermal equilibration and conditioning history.

critical_findings.evidence: The proposal requires median SI to be no greater than E1 values of 0.095 and 0.168 at both windows, although E1 is a single original realization and the payload documents substantial E2 process-state variability. The directly supported local distinction is improvement relative to E5, not guaranteed recovery to E1.
critical_findings.issue: The provisional acceptance criterion is stricter than the evidence supports and may convert the lower-drift E1 reference into an unsupported universal target.

critical_findings.evidence: All candidate scorecards report six missing process fields and high process-history uncertainty. The candidate hypothesis explicitly states that true NCO:OH stoichiometry must be recalculated if acrylic-like or tackifier-like materials contribute reactive groups, but the proposed experiment does not require verified functionality specifications and recalculated stoichiometry as a precondition.
critical_findings.issue: Interpretation remains vulnerable to unresolved stoichiometric and process-history uncertainty in the modified formulation.

critical_findings.evidence: External tackifier evidence clusters around approximately 4.8-6.4 wt% and gives a broad below-10 wt% guidance rule. S1C40 uses 2.5 wt%, and the proposer itself identifies whether this loading is sufficient as unresolved.
critical_findings.issue: The 2.5 wt% tackifier choice is a low-burden extrapolation rather than an independently evidenced sufficiency level.

critical_findings.evidence: S1C40 simultaneously changes acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes. The performance-mitigation intent justifies this design, but any mechanistic or single-axis causal interpretation would be unsupported without separate controls or later experiments.
critical_findings.issue: The two-axis intervention is appropriate for performance mitigation but cannot establish which axis caused any improvement.

critical_findings.evidence: The state-aware model achieved approximately 6-10% pooled multiplicative calibration error only within the original local chemistry family. The payload explicitly limits the shared-shape/state-shift claim to that family, whereas S1C40 introduces two external modifier families.
critical_findings.issue: The state-aware calibration rule is being extended beyond the chemistry family on which it was audited.

critical_findings.evidence: The payload states that the current exact V2 grid and fine-refinement software were formalized after the validation experiment and that no repository freeze artifact is available. This does not demonstrate outcome leakage, but it weakens the claim that the exact candidate ranking procedure was pre-result.
critical_findings.issue: The historical provenance of the candidate grid and minimum-sufficient-intervention implementation is not fully contemporaneously established.

interpretability_failures: The phrase 'substantially altered initial viscosity' is not quantitatively defined, so failure attribution could become post hoc.
The criterion that replicate spread comparable to the E2 process-state spread prevents interpretation lacks a prespecified statistical or numerical threshold.
A single state anchor at 120 C may not distinguish a true state shift from modifier-induced changes in thermal-response shape when the candidate is outside the audited chemistry family.
Without verified modifier functionality and recalculated NCO:OH balance, an observed hold response could reflect altered cure or stoichiometry rather than the intended modifier-family intervention.

leakage_check.detail: No validation formulation identity, wet-lab outcome, or outcome-derived label is visible in the supplied tool results, and the rheology tool states that validation information was not used. However, the payload also states that the exact V2 grid and refinement software were formalized after validation and that no repository freeze artifact exists, leaving provenance of the exact candidate-ranking operationalization uncertain.

regularity_alignment.detail: The proposal correctly prioritizes the measured 120 C thermal-hold drift, separates static viscosity from stability, uses full intervention coverage for a performance-mitigation intent, and retains state calibration and process-history controls. Qualification is required because S1C40 uses a 2.5 wt% tackifier level below the repeated external minor-resin cluster, while the requirement to include both axes is a conservative design rule rather than demonstrated local intervention sufficiency.

required_corrections: Retain S1C40 as the provisional performance candidate, but define success primarily as prespecified improvement relative to E5 at both 15-60 and 15-90 min; treat reaching E1 SI as a favorable secondary benchmark rather than a mandatory threshold.
Prespecify numerical rules for allowable initial-viscosity differences, trajectory comparison, replicate spread, and what constitutes a process-state-confounded result.

Verify modifier OH or other NCO-reactive functionality, recalculate total formulation closure and true NCO:OH stoichiometry, and document all six missing process-history fields before interpreting the result.
Report the 120 C state anchor and full 80-130 C sweep, but label calibration for S1C40 as an extrapolation requiring validation rather than as an established transferable correction.
State explicitly that the dual-modifier result tests a performance-mitigation hypothesis and cannot identify acrylic-versus-tackifier causality.
Preserve S1C41 as a planned robustness comparison if resources permit; otherwise label tackifier sufficiency as unresolved rather than implying that 2.5 wt% is sufficient.
Document the pre-result provenance of the candidate selection and separate directly measured facts from reconstructed conservative decision rules.

scientific_boundary_check.detail: The proposal generally respects the boundary between local measured evidence, external analogue evidence, and conservative design rules. Nevertheless, the state-aware model is extrapolated from the original chemistry family to a dual-modifier formulation, modifier functionality and stoichiometry are unresolved, and the E1-level acceptance threshold is treated more strongly than the local evidence warrants.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

PAT_US6465104B1 Example 10: 25 wt% low-OH acrylic copolymer with direct 121 C viscosity-stability data
PAPER_CN_ADHESIVES_2025_34_09_54: reports a 15% preferred acrylic-resin addition level, retained as directional lower-bound evidence until its fraction denominator is reverified
acrylic_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 20 and 25% are directly commensurate coarse anchors in the current curated record. The 15% grid level is retained as a lower-bound design point, but the literature denominator for the reported 15% addition level is not treated as an exact total-formulation anchor until reverified.

evidence: PAT_US5932680A: examples around 4.8-6.4% tackifying/hydrocarbon resin and preferred resin range 3-10 wt%
PAT_US20070155859A1: tackifiers/rheology-control agents typically used below about 10 wt%
minor_tackifier_like_modifier_pct_total.interpretation: 5% represents the repeatedly documented minor-resin region and 10% is a conservative coarse upper level.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

local_reactive_core_anchor.reason: E2 is the geometric centre of the original five-point local design: 50/50 PPG2000/PDP-70 and NCO:OH=1.80, centered between E1/E3 stoichiometric perturbations and E4/E5 composition perturbations.
local_reactive_core_anchor.stoichiometry_note: The E2 NCO:OH=1.80 label applies to the original reactive core. If a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group, true stoichiometry must be recalculated from verified material specifications.

stability_hypotheses.H1_formulation_family: Partial replacement of the reactive-only formulation by an acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like resin can reduce hot-hold viscosity drift under matched process conditions.
stability_hypotheses.H2_functionality: At comparable acrylic loading, lower effective reactive-group density or lower-OH acrylic chemistry is expected to be more favorable for hot-hold viscosity stability than more highly reactive acrylic chemistry.
stability_hypotheses.H3_region: A useful candidate region is expected within the externally supported coarse space spanned by 15-25% acrylic-like modifier and 0-10% minor tackifier-like modifier, while preserving the relative E2 reactive-core proportions.

tool_trace.name: query_external_priors
tool_trace.reason: Retrieve source-level chemistry evidence to support plausible modifier directions and bounded regions. Use acrylic percentages as directional/noncommensurate anchors and comparative stability reports as hypotheses, not as exact local targets.
